w10_T4_009851: Marcus had 225 dollars in his savings account. He spent 164 dollars on a new computer. A bonus from his job then gave him twice the remaining amount. His grandmother sent him 35 dollars for his birthday. He spent 33 dollars on groceries. When he converted his final amount to 2-dollar bills, how many bills did Marcus have?
w10_T4_009857: Alice started with 80 toy cars in her collection. She divided them in half and gave one half to her friend Ben, keeping 40 for herself. Her mother then bought her 9 cars for each car she had, bringing her total to 360. A collector valued her cars at 4 times the count. The cars were sorted into 6 equal displays. Her final collection was then multiplied by 6. How many cars was Alice's total collection worth?
w10_T4_009861: Sarah had 153 cookies initially. She baked 13 more cookies for the school bake sale. She divided all the cookies in half to share with her classmate Tom. She then arranged them into 7 equal packs. She had twice as many packs as Tom. Over the course of 3 hours (which was not used in the calculation), Sarah had organized all the cookies. How many packs did Sarah end up with?
w10_T4_009863: A warehouse started with 92 boxes of supplies. After a shipment, 49 boxes were sold. The inventory was then multiplied by 7 when new stock arrived (multiplying all remaining items by 7). The count multiplied by 9 during the annual stock take. Finally, 1906 boxes were shipped out. The remaining boxes were grouped into 5 equal warehouses. How many boxes were in each warehouse location?
w10_T4_009865: Elena began with 226 dollars. She earned 10 dollars from babysitting and then 22 dollars from tutoring in the morning. In the afternoon, her earnings tripled (multiplied by 9). In the evening, she received 16 dollars from her grandpa. She then doubled everything she had to prepare for shopping. How many dollars did Elena have at the end of the day?
w10_T4_009867: A shop had 171 items on the shelf. In the morning, 61 items were sold. During the afternoon restock, 67 items arrived. The inventory was then divided equally into 3 storage areas. In the evening, 47 items were removed for display. Finally, 9 items were lost. How many items remained after all the changes?
w10_T4_009870: Jose started with 95 dollars. In the morning, he earned 33 dollars from his paper route. He then earned 31 dollars from mowing lawns. Unfortunately, he spent 119 dollars on a bicycle repair. In the afternoon, he received 24 dollars from a refund. How much money did Jose have left?
w10_T4_009871: A farmer had 171 eggs to sell at the market. He used 120 eggs to make pasta. He then multiplied his remaining product quantity by 4, and then by 8. His production multiplied by 9 to meet demand. He split his shipment equally between 2 distribution centers. Then he split each center's share in half again. How many units did each final location receive?
w10_T4_009876: A factory started with 218 units of production. In the first shift, 53 units were rejected. In the second shift, 117 more units failed quality checks. The remaining good units were multiplied by 6 (representing cases). The total then multiplied by 5. Finally, 974 units were shipped out. How many units were left in storage?
w10_T4_009877: James started his day with 160 dollars. He received 72 dollars from his client for a project. His earnings then multiplied by 5 when his rate was raised. He spent 489 dollars on rent. His account was then credited with 51 dollars. Throughout the transaction, his friend John had 200 dollars (not involved in James's accounting). What was James's final balance?
w10_T4_009879: A bakery had 195 cookies at opening. In the morning rush, sales doubled (multiplied by 2). After the morning, the count was divided by 2 for inventory check. Each of those batches was then multiplied by 8. In the afternoon, the cookies multiplied by 7. By closing, they multiplied by 5 times more. How many cookies did the bakery have at the end of the day?
w10_T4_009884: Linda had 108 dollars on Monday morning. She earned 3 dollars from helping her neighbor. She then earned 8 times that amount from part-time work, giving her significantly more. By Tuesday, she had spent 292 dollars on supplies. She received a check for 78 dollars on Wednesday. She then split her remaining funds equally in half. How much was each half?
w10_T4_009885: David had 146 dollars to start his week. He received 66 dollars from his paycheck. He divided his total money in half and gave one half to his brother (keeping 106 dollars). He subtracted 90 dollars for rent. His remaining amount quadrupled after his tax refund. He then spent 21 dollars on books. Finally, he multiplied his savings by 4. How many dollars did David have finally?
w10_T4_009895: Sarah had 80 dollars at the start of the week. She spent 11 dollars on Tuesday. She earned 72 dollars from freelance work on Wednesday. She then doubled her money with a bonus payment. She earned 3 dollars more from tips. Her total then multiplied by 5. By the end, she multiplied everything by 7 more times (measuring in 7-dollar bundles). How many bundles did Sarah have?
w10_T4_009898: A store had 116 items in stock on Monday morning. By afternoon, 53 items were sold. The store manager added 43 items. The new total multiplied by 6 for inventory purposes. The count decreased by 20 due to damage. Everything then multiplied by 5 for final accounting. Over the day, his assistant had 85 items (not part of this inventory). What was the final inventory count?
w10_T4_009901: Tim had 184 dollars to invest. He tripled his investment money on the first day. He then added 27 dollars from his paycheck. His portfolio multiplied by 7 in value from a stock gain. He added 32 dollars more. His total assets multiplied by 4. How much money did Tim have at the end?
w10_T4_009903: A library had 78 books initially in a donation box. In the morning, 12 books were damaged and removed. During the day, 74 books were added from a new donor. By afternoon, the books were tripled in their cataloging units. Then 56 books were processed. The final amount was reduced by 334 books sent to other libraries. He finally tripled the remainder for special counting. How many books were in the final count?
w10_T4_009907: A project budget started at 215 dollars. In the first quarter, 36 dollars were spent. In the second quarter, 73 dollars were allocated. The amount was then divided in half for two departments. The total multiplied by 6 for annual projections. How much was the final annual projection?
w10_T4_009909: The gym had 219 members at the start of the month. The membership doubled with a promotion (multiplied by 2). Then 50 new members joined. The month saw 115 members leave. Another 7 members canceled. By month-end, 59 new members signed up. His friend who is a trainer had 100 members in his class (separate count). What was the final gym membership?
w10_T4_009921: A bakery started the day with 61 cookies. In the morning, they baked 7 more. Then they made twice as many cookies (doubling the batch). They then divided the cookies into 4 equal packs. Each pack was then divided into 8 individual cookies. Finally, they multiplied by 5 for the display count. How many cookies were in the final display arrangement?
w10_T4_009926: A farmer had 131 apples initially. In the morning harvest, he picked 60 more apples. Then he picked 45 additional apples in the afternoon. He packed them in groups of 4. He then created 3 crates from the groups. Each crate was multiplied by 8 for total storage capacity. How many apples could the storage system hold?
w10_T4_009935: A shop had 22 items at opening. The inventory multiplied by 5 during morning restock. Then 64 items arrived from a supplier. The new total doubled. Finally, 44 more items arrived. How many items were in the shop at the end?
w10_T4_009937: The bank processed 63 transactions. In the morning, 12 were rejected. The remaining valid transactions tripled. Then 32 more were added. In the evening, 36 were reversed. How many transactions remained in the final count?
w10_T4_009942: A child received 36 dollars from relatives. She spent 21 dollars on toys. She tripled her remaining money with a matching gift program. Then she received 50 dollars more. She multiplied her total by 5 for savings goal tracking. How many dollars in her savings goal was set?
w10_T4_009944: A writer had 208 pages written. He multiplied his word count by 5 (in terms of page equivalents). He lost 377 pages in a computer crash. He recovered 32 pages from a backup. His final work was then tripled in length for a special edition. How many pages was the special edition?
